article_title: COVID-19-related differences in students’ verbal achievements: Comparisons of different cohorts of students with SEN based on large-scale assessment data from Germany
citation: Rebecca Schneider, Sebastian Weirich, Poldi Kuhl, Stefan Schipolowski, Petra Stanat. (2025). COVID-19-related differences in students' verbal achievements: Comparisons of different cohorts of students with SEN based on large-scale assessment data from Germany. Learning and Instruction 100 (2025) 102228. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2025.102228
title: IQB Trends in Student Achievement large-scale assessment data (IQB-BT 2021 and IQB-BT 2022)
description: Representative German large-scale educational assessment datasets providing achievement scores in reading, listening, and orthography for cohorts before and after the pandemic restrictions. The article states: "Our analyses are based on data from German large-scale educational assessment studies with achievement scores available for student cohorts prior to the COVID-19 pandemic (T1) and for student cohorts affected by the pandemic-related restrictions (T2)." Sampling used a stratified multi-stage random selection process; items were administered via a multiple matrix sampling design with a Common-Item Nonequivalent Groups Design linking to compare subgroups with different mean ability. Data include student, parent, teacher, and principal questionnaires.
requirements: Case weights to make data representative for students at regular and special needs schools
Multiple imputation and replication procedures for clustered samples in analysis
constraints: The authors state they do not have permission to share the data
target_learners: Grade 4 and Grade 9 students in Germany, including students with SEN-L at regular and special needs schools
target_learning_goals: Verbal competencies in reading, listening, and orthography based on German national educational standards
examples: The IQB-BT 2021 study supplied the Grade 4 2016/2021 cohorts and the IQB-BT 2022 study the Grade 9 2015/2022 cohorts analyzed here
key_sources: Rebecca Schneider, Sebastian Weirich, Poldi Kuhl, Stefan Schipolowski, Petra Stanat. (2025). COVID-19-related differences in students' verbal achievements: Comparisons of different cohorts of students with SEN based on large-scale assessment data from Germany. Learning and Instruction 100 (2025) 102228. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2025.102228

article_title: Novice providers' success in performing lumbar puncture: a randomized controlled phantom study between a conventional spinal needle and a novel bioimpedance needle.
citation: Lilja Helmiina, Talvisara Maria, Eskola Vesa, Heikkilä Paula, Sievänen Harri, Palmu Sauli. (2024). Novice providers' success in performing lumbar puncture: a randomized controlled phantom study between a conventional spinal needle and a novel bioimpedance needle. BMC Medical Education 24:520. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05505-z
title: IQ-Tip bioimpedance spinal needle system with real-time CSF detection
description: The IQ-Tip system (Injeq Plc, Tampere, Finland) is a 90 mm spinal needle that senses tissue bioimpedance at the needle tip. It "provides real-time feedback from the needle tip when penetrating the lumbar tissues and informs the physician when the needle tip reaches CSF with an audio-visual alarm." In the study it was used by novice students on a lumbar phantom, requiring no additional devices such as ultrasound imaging.
requirements: Requires no additional devices beyond the needle system itself; the article states its basic use is virtually similar to a conventional spinal needle with no need for additional devices (e.g., ultrasound imaging).
constraints: In two cases the system did not detect saline although the needle tip was in the correct place, confirmed by saline flow after stylet removal.
One author (H.S.) is an employee of Injeq Plc, the system's manufacturer.
target_learners: early-stage (first- to third-year) medical students with no prior lumbar puncture experience
target_learning_goals: performing lumbar puncture successfully and confidently
examples: In the randomized controlled phantom trial, 30 students performed lumbar puncture with the IQ-Tip system after watching a 25-second animation on how the bioimpedance system operates.
key_sources: Lilja Helmiina, Talvisara Maria, Eskola Vesa, Heikkilä Paula, Sievänen Harri, Palmu Sauli. (2024). Novice providers' success in performing lumbar puncture: a randomized controlled phantom study between a conventional spinal needle and a novel bioimpedance needle. BMC Medical Education 24:520. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05505-z

article_title: Introduction to foundations of probability and randomness (for students in physics), Lectures given at the Institute of Quantum Optics and Quantum Information, Austrian Academy of Science, Lecture-1: Kolmogorov and von Mises
citation: Andrei Khrennikov. (2014). Introduction to foundations of probability and randomness (for students in physics). Lecture-1: Kolmogorov and von Mises. https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.5773
title: Two-lecture foundational probability and randomness course for quantum physics students
description: A pair of black-board lectures given at the Institute of Quantum Optics and Quantum Information in 2014, converted into a written text for students. Lecture 1 covers Kolmogorov axiomatics, observables as random variables, conditional probability, the strong law of large numbers, joint distributions and the Boole-Bell inequality, and von Mises frequency theory; a second lecture covers further randomness approaches and quantum probabilistic data. The author wrote it because students "asked me permanently about foundational problems of probability and randomness".
requirements: Learners need background in quantum information theory, quantum optics, or quantum foundations, where primitive probability treatment causes misunderstandings
constraints: The text is based on lectures originally presented in traditional black-board form and is addressed to students at IQOQI and other young physicists
target_learners: experiment-oriented physics students and young physicists at IQOQI and similar institutions
target_learning_goals: understand foundational problems of probability and randomness and the inter-relation between classical and quantum structures
examples: Lecture 1 develops the Kolmogorov and von Mises frameworks with historical remarks, worked examples such as the three-point probability space, and place-selection examples
key_sources: Andrei Khrennikov. (2014). Introduction to foundations of probability and randomness (for students in physics). Lecture-1: Kolmogorov and von Mises. https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.5773

article_title: On-Premises Superconducting Quantum Computer for Education and Research
citation: Jami Rönkkö, Olli Ahonen, Ville Bergholm, Alessio Calzona, Attila Geresdi, Hermanni Heimonen, Johannes Heinsoo, Vladimir Milchakov, Stefan Pogorzalek, Matthew Sarsby, Mykhailo Savytskyi, Stefan Seegerer, Fedor Šimkovic IV, P.V. Sriluckshmy, Panu T. Vesanen, Mikio Nakahara (2024). On-Premises Superconducting Quantum Computer for Education and Research. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07315
title: IQM Spark prototype: a 5-qubit on-premises superconducting quantum computer with full hardware and software stack
description: The article introduces an on-premises full-stack superconducting quantum computer, "a 5-qubit superconducting quantum computer designed and developed to enable a low-barrier access to both its hardware and software components." It integrates a five-qubit QPU with tunable couplers, a dilution refrigerator, parametric-amplifier readout, control electronics, and a layered software stack (Cortex, EXA, IQM Station Control) supporting pulse-level and circuit-level access for education and research.
requirements: Operation requires a dilution refrigerator; the experiments were performed with components attached to a stage at 30 mK or cooler
Calibration is required to find the optimal parameters to operate the QPU and is crucial for high fidelity operations
constraints: The reported system is a research prototype; the article states its specifications and performance may differ from the commercial IQM Spark TM
target_learners: university students in quantum computing and quantum hardware courses
target_learning_goals: running and mitigating quantum algorithms on NISQ hardware
examples: Cortex lets users define and execute quantum algorithms expressed in Cirq, Qiskit, and OpenQASM 2.0
EXA supports pre-defined and custom experiments for characterising, calibrating, and controlling the quantum computer
key_sources: Jami Rönkkö, Olli Ahonen, Ville Bergholm, Alessio Calzona, Attila Geresdi, Hermanni Heimonen, Johannes Heinsoo, Vladimir Milchakov, Stefan Pogorzalek, Matthew Sarsby, Mykhailo Savytskyi, Stefan Seegerer, Fedor Šimkovic IV, P.V.
